Third straight fall and the first trade below Monday's $99.76 low, on recovering Middle East exports. PVM: Brent's reasons for trading much beyond $100 are being eroded (Rigzone). The rupee did not respond today, but a settle below $100 lowers the import bill if it holds
Back under 102 after Monday's 102.54 high as lower oil eased inflation and rate-hike worries; the euro recovered 0.5%. PTI quoted 102.03 at the Indian close. USD/JPY 158.20

Paused after Monday's 24-year high (TE 5.33%; Investing.com 5.351 high, 5.304 close). A Fed hold on 28 Oct is ~78% priced, with a hike expected in December. Still above 5.25% — the level keeping foreign money out of Indian assets. FOMC minutes Wed night

factors.lv: Record ~$77bn of importer forwards in September

Equity outflows (FIIs sold ₹4,699 crore on Monday) and record importer hedging did the damage, and state-bank dollar sales only slowed it. Importers: buy dips to 96.25–96.35, stop-hedge above 96.60. Exporters: sell 96.50–96.65, more near 96.80.

ISM services 54.9 vs 55.0 expected and 55.4 prior, but prices paid rose to 74.0 from 72.6 and employment to 50.1 (Investrade). A Fed hold on 28 Oct is ~78% priced; the long end is selling off anyway. FOMC minutes tomorrow night
Broke the 102.21 high of 1 Oct intraday. TE: strongest since April 2025, with the euro under pressure from French fiscal concerns and Spain's snap election. USD/JPY 157.93

Fell on Aramco's Asian price cut and exports recovering toward pre-war levels. ANZ sees $95–100, with ~$110 on escalation. Lowest settle since 30 Sep — trims the import bill, but Brent has not yet closed below $100
The RBI is acting as a buffer and held Monday's range to 11 paise, but traders say it may not defend a specific level if pressure persists. Reserves $747.56bn (25 Sep); next print Fri 9 Oct
factors.lv: Dollar sales stepped up; no hard line expected

factors.d: India 10Y 7.217%, two-year highs. A hike with firm guidance supports carry; a hold or dovish hike with the US 10Y at 5.3% would open 96.50–96.80 quickly

Trump says the war is essentially almost over. A Saudi-led coalition hit 324 Houthi targets and Yemeni forces claim Bab el-Mandeb (Fox News). No confirmed loss of output, so crude ignored it — but it is why Brent holds $100
factors.lv: Third tanker hit in 48h; Pezeshkian: talks meaningless; Houthis claim Rabigh refinery strike

factors.lv: GIFT Nifty 22,639.50 (+18 pts); Nasdaq +1.05% to a record, S&P 500 +0.66%

factors.lv: Brent settled $101.08 (+0.76%) after a $97.09 low; ~$101.4 in Asia. WTI $89.91, ~$90.1

Tuesday range 101.76–102.29; closed off the low as oil rebounded. Trading Economics shows 102.01 on Wednesday, EUR/USD 1.1238, USD/JPY 158.39, USD/CNY 6.703. Below Monday's 102.54 high, but not falling

First draw after three weekly builds; it helped crude hold its rebound. Official EIA data is due tonight. Gains were limited by reports of Gulf flows returning toward pre-war levels and the G7 stock release

factors.d: Dow 51,521.28 (+0.49%), Nasdaq 27,599.79 (+0.45%). GIFT Nifty (EquityPandit, 02:00 IST) points to a flat open after the Nifty's 22,776.10 close. FII flow for 6 Oct was not available. India 10Y 7.197% (TE). Gold $4,141 (−0.56%)

oil.detail: Iranian supply is fully off the market even as other Gulf flows recover toward pre-war levels (TE); markets doubt the recovery lasts without an agreement. Supports the risk premium in Brent — mildly bearish INR.
oil.headline: Iran loaded zero crude barrels onto tankers in September under the US 'Operation Economic Outcast'

oil.detail: East-West pipeline (7 mb/d) still partially offline after the 10 Sep drone attacks. Recovering Gulf crude flows cap Brent's upside and are mildly rupee-supportive, though the market doubts they hold without a deal.
oil.headline: Saudi crude shipments through Hormuz rose to 2.9 mb/d in September from 1 mb/d in August — highest since the war began

oil.detail: USS Theodore Roosevelt group and the 13th MEU are due by end-November. Markets read it as escalation risk; with China's fuel-export halt it pushed Brent to $102.31. Crude above $100 is directly rupee-negative and keeps USD/INR 96+ in play.
oil.headline: US sends third carrier strike group and ~10,000 sailors and Marines to the Middle East; Brent settles +4.4% above $102

oil.headline: Brent recovers from $98.40 to settle $102.25 on Friday, up ~3.5% on the week; WTI $91.26, down ~1.2%

oil.headline: G7 agrees to release 100 mb through the IEA over four months, diesel front-loaded in the first 20 days

oil.headline: Kpler: three-quarters of pre-war volumes now moving via Hormuz and Yanbu; diesel remains the pinch point

The cut offsets record freight (VLCCs ~$1.2m/day vs ~$80,000 a year ago), longer voyages and loading delays at Sidi Kerir. For India it lowers the delivered cost of Saudi barrels even with Brent above $100 — a small positive for the import bill and INR.
oil.headline: Saudi Aramco unexpectedly cuts November Arab Light to Asia by $3 to $5 below Oman/Dubai, a six-year low

oil.detail: Brent opened the week at $103.09 on Sunday and eased to ~$101.4–101.9 on Monday; WTI ~$90. Murban at a ~$9 premium to Brent shows Gulf-to-Asia delivered crude — India's relevant grade — is still costlier than the futures suggest, on freight, insurance and tanker shortages.
oil.headline: Brent slips toward $101.6 in Asia after the OPEC+ hold while Murban trades $110.80; Brent–WTI spread above $11

oil.detail: Trading Economics: markets are balancing easing supply (Aramco's deeper Asian discount, G7 stock releases, East-West pipeline operating normally) against Middle East risk and the OPEC+ hold. oil.detail: Smoke and flames were seen near an Aramco site in Riyadh, but no damage or output loss is confirmed. A new front for the risk premium: any verified hit to Saudi processing would lift Brent quickly and pressure the rupee.
oil.headline: Houthis claim missile and drone strikes on Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais; Saudi coalition calls the claims misleading

oil.detail: Gives SOMO more flexibility on sales and pricing and adds to evidence that Gulf flows are recovering (Business Standard: West Asia exports back at pre-war levels in late September). Supportive for the rupee at the margin.

oil.headline: Tanker entering Hormuz reverses course after IRGC threat, 11 nm north of Khasab

oil.headline: OPEC+ keeps November output targets unchanged; next meeting 1 November

timeline.read: Tuesday changed what is driving the pair. Oil, the dollar and US yields all eased — Brent to ~$97.7, the dollar index to ~101.8, the 10Y to 5.27% — and the rupee still closed at 96.42, a two-month low, after trading 96.29–96.45. The pressure came from equity outflows and importers' forward buying, with state-bank dollar sales only slowing it. So the near-term question is no longer oil; it is whether the RBI's decision on 7 Oct gives foreigners and hedgers a reason to stop buying dollars. A 25bp hike with firm guidance should hold the pair in 96.05–96.70 and lets cheaper crude start to show; a hold, which roughly 40% of economists expect, would likely send it to 96.80–97.00 quickly. Beyond that, US CPI (14 Oct), the FOMC (27–28 Oct) and the 3 Nov midterms set the medium-term tails. A Hormuz deal remains the only catalyst big enough to pull the pair back toward 95.
